title: Bounded derived-complete integral geometric stalks
statement: For a geometric point y of Y and an integral complex K as in [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], suppose K is derived complete in the sense of [def-weil-derived-complete] and all derived finite reductions have cohomological support in the same interval [a,b], a <= b. The termwise integral module stalk C, with the constant integral scalar action of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], has finite cohomological support and Q(C) is derived complete for the ideal generated by the lifted uniformizer.

from.place: Proof, final paragraph: derived-complete integral stalk and the common reduction bounds

proof.text: The abelian geometric stalk is isomorphic to evaluation at the pointed strict localization by the classical stalk theorem. Evaluation preserves products. Forgetting module scalars detects limits, so the integral module stalk preserves countable products; the same comparison makes it exact.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: derived-complete integral stalk and the common reduction bounds

proof.text: Module sheaves and modules have exact countable products. Consequently Q and homology preserve countable products, and the exact derived stalk preserves them as well. Apply the exact-functor Roos argument to the defining completeness triangle. Transport its limit object to Q of the termwise stalk using the exact-derived-functor comparison.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: derived-complete integral stalk and the common reduction bounds

proof.text: An element r in the uniformizer ideal has r^(n+1)=0 in the nth quotient. The constant-to-completion map followed by the nth projection is the constant quotient map. On colimit representatives this gives r^(n+1) times identity zero on the stalk of the restricted nth reduction. Restriction and stalk are exact, hence the same vanishing holds in the derived category. Apply the nilpotent reduction-limit criterion to the transported Roos triangle.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: derived-complete integral stalk and the common reduction bounds

proof.text: Exactness identifies the cohomology of each reduction stalk with the stalk of its cohomology, so all lie in [a,b]. Homology preserves countable products. In the long exact sequence of the Roos triangle both adjacent product cohomologies vanish outside [a,b+1]. The limit therefore has finite cohomological support.

theorem integralStalk_roos_control
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y)
    (K : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E Y) ℤ)
    (hcomplete : IsSfDerivedComplete l E Y (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K))
    (a b : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b)
    (hbound : ∀ n : ℕ, proEtaleCohomologicalSupport
      ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E Y n).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) ⊆ Set.Icc a b) :
    let R := ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)
    let I : Ideal R := Ideal.span {ULift.up (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)}
    let C := DerivedCategory.Q.obj
      (((integralCoefficientModuleStalkFunctor l E y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K)
    (∃ s : Finset ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ∉ s →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) i).obj C)) ∧
      DerivedCategory.IsDerivedComplete I C
